abstract: The ex utero intrapartum treatment (EXIT) procedure is a rare form of perinatal resuscitation. It is basically a bridge therapy between partial delivery of the child and stabilization of its cardiorespiratory functions. This procedure has multiple anesthetic challenges including maternal anesthesia, maintenance of uteroplacental flow, tocolysis till the neonate is stabilized, management of postpartum hemorrhage, fetal, and neonatal anesthesia. This review also describes a case of cervical teratoma in fetus, for which the EXIT was performed in our institute. In addition to the case description, multiple concerns specific for EXIT procedure are discussed in this review.
abstract_ja: ex utero intrapartum treatment(EXIT)手技は、まれな周産期蘇生法である。基本的には、児の部分娩出と心肺機能の安定化の間をつなぐ橋渡し療法である。本手技には、母体麻酔、子宮胎盤血流の維持、新生児が安定するまでの子宮収縮抑制(tocolysis)、産後出血の管理、胎児および新生児麻酔など、多くの麻酔上の課題がある。本総説では、当施設で EXIT が実施された胎児の頸部奇形腫の症例についても記述する。症例の記述に加え、EXIT 手技に特有の多くの懸念事項について考察する。
